week_in_brief: Real estate brokerages are leaning into AI-assisted lead nurturing as inventory constraints keep transaction volumes suppressed and the fight for buyer attention intensifies.

items.headline: Brokerages using AI-powered lead response are converting 28% more inquiries into appointments
items.tag: 🏠 LEAD GEN | AI Nurture Sequences Cut Time-to-Contact From Days to Minutes
items.whats_happening: The data is unambiguous: the window between a buyer submitting an inquiry and making contact with an agent is collapsing. Brokerages with AI-assisted instant response — even just an intelligent first-touch text or email — are locking in the conversation before competitors can respond.
items.so_what: If your brokerage client is still relying on agents to manually follow up with web leads, they're losing deals to whoever responds first. The floor here is an automated first-touch sequence. The ceiling is a full AI pre-qualification flow that hands warm leads to agents.

items.headline: Real estate advertisers on Meta are generating buyer leads at $18–32 CPL vs. $55–80 on Google for equivalent zip codes
items.tag: 📊 PAID SOCIAL | Meta Remains the ROI Leader for Buyer Acquisition
items.whats_happening: Despite platform headwinds, Meta's targeting efficiency for real estate buyer acquisition remains significantly better than Google in most markets. The combination of interest-based and lookalike targeting continues to outperform search intent alone for early-funnel buyers.
items.so_what: For clients still over-indexed on Google search, this is a reallocation conversation worth having. A 60/40 Meta/Google split typically outperforms 100% Google for buyer lead volume at the same budget. The caveat: Meta leads require faster and better nurture — they're higher-volume but lower-intent.

items.headline: Individual agent content on LinkedIn and Instagram is generating 4–6x more local engagement than brokerage brand accounts
items.tag: 🔑 BRAND | Agent Personal Branding Is Outperforming Brokerage Brand in Local Markets
items.whats_happening: Buyers and sellers are increasingly choosing agents, not brands. In local markets especially, agent-led content — market updates, neighborhood guides, behind-the-scenes closings — is dramatically outperforming generic brokerage content in both reach and engagement.
items.so_what: The opportunity for brokerage clients is to systematize agent content rather than fight it. Build a content toolkit agents can actually use: templated market update videos, neighborhood spotlight formats, social-ready stats. The brokerage wins when the agents win.

this_weeks_take: The brokerage market is in a weird spot — transaction volume is still suppressed, but buyer demand hasn't evaporated, it's just fragmented across more channels and more agents competing for the same leads. The brokerages pulling ahead are the ones who've systematized the lead-to-appointment journey (AI nurture + fast response) and given their agents tools to build personal brand at scale. The ones still waiting for inventory to recover without changing their marketing approach are going to find themselves further behind when the market does loosen.
